claims.text: Ambient-air-debound additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit non-uniform dimensions.
Ambient air debinding produces oxide inclusions in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Vacuum debinding before solid-state sintering reduces oxidation relative to ambient air debinding.
Vacuum debinding promotes more uniform inter-particle necking during subsequent sintering.
Vacuum debinding minimizes oxygen exposure during binder removal.
Minimizing oxygen exposure suppresses brittle oxide-layer formation at particle interfaces.
Cleaner particle surfaces promote diffusion during solid-state sintering.
Cleaner particle surfaces improve inter-particle bonding during solid-state sintering.
Improved diffusion and inter-particle bonding increase dimensional stability.
Improved diffusion and inter-particle bonding increase mechanical strength.
Vacuum-debound components will have lower oxide content than ambient-air-debound controls.
Vacuum-debound components will have tighter dimensional tolerances than ambient-air-debound controls.
Vacuum-debound components will have greater tensile strength than ambient-air-debound controls.
Vacuum-debound components will have greater fracture toughness than ambient-air-debound controls.
The proposed improvement should occur when vacuum debinding is conducted below approximately 10^-2 torr before conventional solid-state sintering.
The benefit of vacuum debinding will be greatest for oxidation-sensitive high-entropy alloys.
Reintroduction of oxygen during later processing can diminish the benefit of vacuum debinding.
Alloy compositions that inherently minimize oxidation effects may receive less benefit from vacuum debinding.
